headline: Approved pavilion replacement at 431 West Cherry Street; continued flood pump station and 5 Appleton Street items to November 12.
summary: The meeting also extended the Bray Lake Trail permit to 2028 and approved minutes from four earlier meetings. No vote was taken on a one-month removal extension requested for 233 Easthampton Road. No further work may be done at 5 Appleton Street until DEP, Heritage and the railroad have responded.
decisions: Approved a negative determination for slab replacement and a pavilion at 431 West Cherry Street, 4-0.
Approved extending the Bray Lake Trail Order of Conditions to 2028, 4-0.
Continued the flood pump station Notice of Intent hearing to November 12, 2026, 4-0.
Continued the 5 Appleton Street enforcement order to November 12, 2026, and required no further work until DEP, Heritage and the railroad respond, 4-0.
No vote was taken on a one-month removal extension requested for 233 Easthampton Road.
Approved minutes of August 13, August 27, September 24, and October 8, 2026, with minor edits, 4-0.

decision_evidence.quote: Vice Chairperson Moriarty moved to issue a Negative Determination under Box 3 for removal and replacement of the slab and installation of the pavilion, with the replacement slab 10 feet shorter and outside the 50-foot buffer. ...The motion carried unanimously, 4-0, by roll call.

Vice Chairperson Moriarty moved to extend the Order of Conditions to the date in 2028 corresponding to the state statutory extension. Commissioner Normand seconded. The motion carried unanimously, 4-0, by roll call.
Commissioner Normand moved to continue the hearing to November 12, 2026. Commissioner Perdrizet seconded. The motion carried unanimously, 4-0, by roll call.

Commissioner Normand moved to continue the matter until November 12 and to require that no further work be done until the Holyoke Conservation Commission hears back from DEP, Heritage and the railroad. ...The motion carried unanimously, 4-0, by roll call.
The Commission took no vote on the extension request.

Vice Chairperson Moriarty moved to approve the minutes of August 13, August 27, September 24, and October 8, 2026, with the minor edits discussed. Commissioner Normand seconded. The motion carried unanimously, 4-0, by roll call.
